_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: Edward William Lane (1801-1876). The Thousand and One Nights (1838-40), as re-edited by E. S. Poole 1859 and reprinted unchanged. PD. Added 2026-10-02 by lane C after the coordinator's 'keep going, more translator shelves' relay; Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted in the relay burst.

lane-nights-1: The Thousand and One Nights, tr. Lane, vol. I (Chatto 1912 impression)

lane-nights-2: The Thousand and One Nights, tr. Lane, vol. II (Chatto 1912)
lane-nights-3: The Thousand and One Nights, tr. Lane, vol. III (Routledge 1865)

lane-arabian-nights.work: The Thousand and One Nights, 3 vols
lane-arabian-nights.scan_edition: vol. 1 PG (Chatto 1912), vol. 2 Chatto 1912, vol. 3 Routledge 1865; the 1912 impression says it reproduces the 1859 edition exactly, so the mix is one text

_pending.lane-selections-kuran: Selections from the Kur-an (PG 44515): Lane as translator of Quranic passages; Adam's call whether scripture of other faiths belongs on a translator shelf.

_excluded.pg-41110: Arabian Society in the Middle Ages: Lane's notes, not a translation.
_excluded.ia-emory-1883: Chatto 1883 set (emory.edu): its text files are not at the standard path.

_name_words_note: Translator name(s) only: fetch_shelf.py treats these as the identity check (one must appear in the fetched text), so the original author's name is deliberately NOT listed.

_identity_checked.lane-nights-2: OCR spreads the name over several spaces ('Edward  William  Lane'), so the exact-phrase check misses it; the title page names him. Checked 2026-10-02.
_identity_checked.lane-nights-3: OCR spreads the name over several spaces ('Edward  William  Lane'), so the exact-phrase check misses it; the title page names him. Checked 2026-10-02.

_verified_note: Evidence that each source's rights/identity line was read (lane C review fix, 2026-10-02, pipeline run over the fetched files; no book text recorded). PG: the header's Translator: line and the COPYRIGHTED marker. IA: whether the translator's name appears in the first 30 KB of OCR, and the years printed in the first 15 KB of front matter (scanner/digitizer lines skipped). Any post-1930 year there was examined by eye; see the title's scan_edition.
